title: CUET Political Science Test 7
subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
syllabus_source: CUET SYLLABUS/Political Science - 323.pdf (NTA syllabus for CUET (UG) 2026, latest published)
past_paper_reference: Pattern benchmark only: NTA CUET (UG) Political Science papers 2024 and 2026, analysed for format only (no questions copied)

instructions: Each correct answer earns 5 marks; each incorrect answer deducts 1 mark; unattempted questions earn 0.
One set of 5 questions is based on a passage; the set stays together.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.sub_topic: Environmental problems and their causes
questions.question:
Match List-I (Problem) with List-II (Main cause).

List-I
(A) Ozone depletion
(B) Acid rain
(C) Loss of biodiversity
(D) Desertification

List-II
(I) Overgrazing and the loss of fertile land
(II) Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)
(III) Destruction of forests
(IV) Sulphur and nitrogen oxides from burning fuel
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(III), (D)-(I)
Why: CFCs deplete the ozone layer (II). Sulphur and nitrogen oxides cause acid rain (IV). Forest destruction causes loss of biodiversity (III). Overgrazing leads to desertification (I).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps ozone depletion and acid rain. Option (C) swaps acid rain and biodiversity loss. Option (D) swaps biodiversity loss and desertification.
Key point: Each environmental problem has human causes.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Alternative Centres of Economic and Political Power
questions.sub_topic: Countries and organisations in the new centres of power
questions.question:
Match List-I (Country or organisation) with List-II (Feature).

List-I
(A) Japan
(B) South Korea
(C) ASEAN
(D) European Union

List-II
(I) Founded by the Bangkok Declaration of 1967
(II) Its economy in 2005 was slightly larger than that of the United States
(III) Contributes about 10 per cent of the UN's regular budget
(IV) Home to companies such as Samsung, LG and Hyundai
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Japan pays about 10 per cent of the UN's regular budget (III). Samsung, LG and Hyundai are South Korean (IV). ASEAN was founded by the Bangkok Declaration (I). The EU's economy in 2005 was slightly larger than the USA's (II).
Why not the others: Option (B) swaps Japan and South Korea. Option (C) swaps South Korea and ASEAN. Option (D) swaps ASEAN and the EU.
Key point: Economic power has spread beyond the superpowers.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.sub_topic: Country that hosted the Earth Summit
questions.question: The Earth Summit of 1992 was held at Rio de Janeiro in which country?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Brazil
Why: Rio de Janeiro is in Brazil.
Why not the others: (A), (B), (D) The summit was not held in these countries.
Key point: Rio put the environment at the centre of world politics.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Alternative Centres of Economic and Political Power
questions.sub_topic: Cities destroyed by nuclear bombs in 1945
questions.question: Japan is the only country to have suffered the destruction caused by nuclear bombs. Which cities were bombed in 1945?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Hiroshima and Nagasaki
Why: The USA dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August 1945.
Why not the others: (B), (C), (D) These cities were not the targets of the atomic bombs.
Key point: Japan rebuilt itself as an economic power after 1945.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.sub_topic: A major concern of indigenous peoples
questions.question: Which of the following is a major concern of indigenous peoples around the world?
options: A) Losing their permanent seats in the UN Security Council
B) The high cost of imported luxury cars in their regions
C) A shortage of software engineers in their home towns
D) Displacement by dams, mines and big projects
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Displacement by dams, mines and big projects
Why: Indigenous peoples have often been displaced from their lands by development projects, losing their homes and livelihoods.
Why not the others: (A), (B), (C) These are not the concerns NCERT describes.
Key point: Indigenous peoples demand rights over land and resources.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Nation-Building and Its Problems
questions.sub_topic: Year the States Reorganisation Commission was appointed
questions.question: In which year did the Central Government appoint the States Reorganisation Commission?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 1953
Why: The Commission was appointed in 1953; its report led to the States Reorganisation Act of 1956.
Why not the others:
(B) 1947 is the year of Independence.
(C) 1960 is when Maharashtra and Gujarat were formed.
(D) 1966 is when Punjab and Haryana were formed.
Key point: The Commission accepted that boundaries should reflect languages.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Regional Aspirations and Conflicts
questions.sub_topic: Which is NOT a lesson of regional aspirations
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the lessons NCERT draws from India's experience of regional aspirations?
options: A) Regional aspirations are part of democratic politics.
B) The best response to every regional demand is force.
C) Democratic negotiation is the way to deal with regional demands.
D) Regional imbalances in development need attention.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) The best response to every regional demand is force.
Why: NCERT stresses negotiation and accommodation, not force, as the right response.
Why not the others: (A), (C), (D) These are lessons NCERT draws.
Key point: Accommodation has strengthened Indian democracy.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.sub_topic: Organs of the United Nations
questions.question:
Match List-I (UN organ) with List-II (Function).

List-I
(A) Economic and Social Council
(B) Trusteeship Council
(C) Secretariat
(D) Security Council

List-II
(I) Supervised territories placed under UN trusteeship
(II) Maintains international peace and security
(III) Deals with economic and social questions
(IV) Runs the UN's daily work under the Secretary-General
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
Why: ECOSOC handles economic and social questions (III). The Trusteeship Council supervised trust territories (I). The Secretariat runs daily work (IV). The Security Council keeps peace and security (II).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps ECOSOC and the Trusteeship Council. Option (B) swaps the Trusteeship Council and the Secretariat. Option (C) swaps the Secretariat and the Security Council.
Key point: The UN has six principal organs with different roles.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.sub_topic: Why Gorbachev's reforms ended in collapse
questions.question: Why did Gorbachev's reforms end in the collapse of the Soviet Union?
options: A) They returned all real power to the Communist Party leadership.
B) They led to an invasion of the Soviet Union by NATO forces.
C) They abolished elections in all of the Soviet republics.
D) They raised hopes and freed forces the leaders could not control.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) They raised hopes and freed forces the leaders could not control.
Why: Reforms let people speak freely and raised their hopes, but the leadership could not meet them; nationalism and protest then broke the union apart.
Why not the others:
(A) The reforms weakened the Party's grip.
(B) There was no NATO invasion.
(C) Elections were extended, not abolished.
Key point: Reform from above unleashed demands from below.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Alternative Centres of Economic and Political Power
questions.sub_topic: Asia and Europe, 1967–2002, in order
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
(A) Rajiv Gandhi visits China
(B) Euro notes and coins come into use
(C) ASEAN is founded
(D) China announces its open-door policy
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (C), (D), (A), (B)
Why: (C) ASEAN was founded in 1967. (D) China's open-door policy came in 1978. (A) Rajiv Gandhi visited China in 1988. (B) The euro came into use in 2002.
Why not the others: Option (A) puts 1978 before 1967. Option (B) puts 1988 before 1978. Option (D) puts the euro before Rajiv Gandhi's visit.
Key point: 1967 → 1978 → 1988 → 2002.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Security in the Contemporary World
questions.sub_topic: Ideas in the new thinking on security — which hold
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Human security puts the protection of people above the protection of states.
(B) Global threats such as climate change need international cooperation.
(C) Terrorism means political violence that deliberately targets civilians.
(D) Refugees are people who flee war or persecution across international borders.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B), (C) and (D)
Why: All four are true. Human security focuses on people (A). Global threats need cooperation (B). Terrorism targets civilians (C). Refugees cross borders, while internally displaced people stay inside their country (D).
Why not the others: Options (A), (B) and (D) each leave out at least one true statement.
Key point: Non-traditional security widens what counts as a threat.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Democratic Upsurge and Coalition Politics
questions.sub_topic: Governments of 2004–2019 in order
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
(A) The BJP wins a majority on its own
(B) The Congress-led UPA forms its first government
(C) The BJP-led NDA returns with a larger majority
(D) The UPA wins a second term
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (B), (D), (A), (C)
Why: (B) The UPA formed its first government in 2004. (D) It won a second term in 2009. (A) The BJP won a majority on its own in 2014. (C) The NDA returned with a larger majority in 2019.
Why not the others: Option (B) puts 2009 before 2004. Option (C) puts 2014 before 2009. Option (D) puts 2019 before 2014.
Key point: 2004 → 2009 → 2014 → 2019.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Politics of Planned Development
questions.sub_topic: Achievements and criticisms of early planning — which hold
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) The Second Plan protected domestic industry by putting high tariffs on imports.
(B) The First Five Year Plan gave top priority to heavy industry.
(C) Early planning laid foundations for growth, including big projects such as the Bhakra Nangal dam.
(D) Critics argued that state control led to corruption and inefficiency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (C) and (D) only
Why: (A) the Second Plan protected industry with tariffs. (C) planning built big dams and industries. (D) critics blamed state control for corruption and inefficiency.
Why not the others: (B) is false: the First Plan focused on agriculture; heavy industry was the Second Plan's priority. Options (B) and (D) include (B); option (A) leaves out (D).
Key point: Planning brought both foundations and problems.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Era of One-Party Dominance
questions.sub_topic: Socialists and Communists, 1934–1957, in order
questions.question:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
(A) The Socialists leave the Congress
(B) The Congress Socialist Party is formed within the Congress
(C) The CPI forms a government in Kerala
(D) The first general election is completed
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (B), (A), (D), (C)
Why: (B) The Congress Socialist Party was formed in 1934. (A) The Socialists left the Congress in 1948. (D) The first general election was completed in 1952. (C) The CPI formed a government in Kerala in 1957.
Why not the others: Option (B) puts 1948 before 1934. Option (C) puts the election before the Socialists left. Option (D) puts Kerala before the first election.
Key point: 1934 → 1948 → 1952 → 1957.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Crises of the Constitutional Order
questions.sub_topic: Terms linked with the Emergency and the courts
questions.question:
Match List-I (Term) with List-II (Meaning).

List-I
(A) Committed judiciary
(B) Basic structure doctrine
(C) MISA
(D) Twenty-Point Programme

List-II
(I) A law used for preventive detention
(II) Judges who favour the ruling party's policies
(III) Indira Gandhi's economic programme announced during the Emergency
(IV) Parliament cannot change the core features of the Constitution
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)
Why: A committed judiciary means judges loyal to the government's policies (II). The basic structure doctrine protects the Constitution's core (IV). MISA was used for preventive detention (I). The Twenty-Point Programme was announced during the Emergency (III).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps the first two terms. Option (B) swaps the doctrine and MISA. Option (C) swaps MISA and the programme.
Key point: The Emergency was also a struggle between the government and the courts.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Globalisation and Its Critics
questions.sub_topic: A basic feature of globalisation
questions.question: Which word best describes the basic idea of globalisation?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Interconnectedness
Why: Globalisation means growing interconnectedness through flows across the world.
Why not the others: (A), (B), (C) These are the opposite of globalisation.
Key point: Flows of ideas, capital, goods and people link the world.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Democratic Upsurge and Coalition Politics
questions.sub_topic: Prime Minister of the National Front government
questions.question: Who was Prime Minister of the National Front government formed in 1989?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) V.P. Singh
Why: V.P. Singh led the National Front government, which had outside support from the BJP and the Left.
Why not the others:
(A) Chandra Shekhar followed in 1990.
(B) Rajiv Gandhi's Congress lost in 1989.
(D) Vajpayee became Prime Minister in 1996.
Key point: 1989 began the era of coalitions.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.sub_topic: How India met its food shortage in the mid-1960s
questions.question: During the food crisis of the mid-1960s, India had to import food grains from the United States under:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) the PL-480 scheme
Why: India imported large amounts of food from the USA under the PL-480 scheme.
Why not the others:
(A) The Marshall Plan helped Western Europe.
(B) The Colombo Plan was a Commonwealth aid scheme, not the food imports NCERT describes.
(D) The Bombay Plan was drafted by Indian industrialists.
Key point: Food dependence pushed India towards the Green Revolution.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: South Asia in the Post-Cold War Era
questions.sub_topic: Expansion of the regional body's name
questions.question: SAARC is an abbreviation. Which of these is its correct expansion?
options: A) South Asian Alliance for Regional Commerce
B) South Asian Agreement on Regional Customs
C) Southern Asian Association for Rural Cooperation
D) South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation
Why: SAARC is the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation.
Why not the others: (A), (B), (C) These are not its name.
Key point: SAARC seeks cooperation through peaceful means.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.sub_topic: Leader who left the Congress and headed Uttar Pradesh in 1967
questions.question: Which leader left the Congress in 1967 and became Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh at the head of a non-Congress coalition?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Charan Singh
Why: Charan Singh left the Congress and headed the non-Congress coalition in Uttar Pradesh in 1967.
Why not the others:
(B) Morarji Desai stayed in the Congress until the split.
(C) Lohia led the Socialists but did not head the State.
(D) Jagjivan Ram left the Congress only in 1977.
Key point: Defections made the SVD governments possible.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: South Asia in the Post-Cold War Era
questions.sub_topic: A reason democracy struggled in Pakistan
questions.question: Which of the following is a reason NCERT gives for the difficulties of democracy in Pakistan?
options: A) Pakistan has never held any general elections since independence.
B) India's army has long controlled the government of Pakistan.
C) There has been little real international support for democratic rule.
D) Pakistan has no political parties apart from the military's own.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) There has been little real international support for democratic rule.
Why: Western powers, including the USA, often backed military rulers for their own interests, so democracy got little real international support.
Why not the others:
(A) Pakistan has held elections.
(B) India has no role in Pakistan's government.
(D) Pakistan has many parties.
Key point: Internal and external factors both weakened democracy in Pakistan.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.sub_topic: Last leader of the Soviet Union
questions.question: Who was the last leader of the Soviet Union?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Mikhail Gorbachev
Why: Gorbachev led the Soviet Union until it was dissolved in December 1991.
Why not the others:
(B) Brezhnev died in 1982.
(C) Yeltsin led Russia, not the USSR.
(D) Khrushchev was removed in 1964.
Key point: Gorbachev's reforms ended in the union's collapse.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.sub_topic: Why Central Asia matters to world powers
questions.question: Why have the Central Asian republics drawn the attention of outside powers since 1991?
options: A) They are the largest exporters of rice in the world.
B) They hold permanent seats in the UN Security Council.
C) They have vast reserves of oil and natural gas.
D) They have the biggest armies in Asia.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) They have vast reserves of oil and natural gas.
Why: Central Asia's large hydrocarbon reserves have made it a zone of competition among outside powers.
Why not the others:
(A) They are not major rice exporters.
(B) Only Russia among the former republics holds a permanent seat.
(D) Their armies are not the biggest in Asia.
Key point: Resources shape great-power interest in Central Asia.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.sub_topic: Another country seeking a permanent seat
questions.question: Like India, which of the following countries seeks a permanent seat in a reformed Security Council?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Brazil
Why: Brazil, along with India, Germany and Japan, seeks a permanent seat.
Why not the others: (A), (C), (D) These countries are not leading claimants for permanent seats.
Key point: Many argue the Council should reflect today's world.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: South Asia in the Post-Cold War Era
questions.sub_topic: A cause of friction between India and Nepal
questions.question: Which of the following has been a cause of friction between India and Nepal?
options: A) Nepal's warm relations with China
B) Nepal's claim to the Siachen glacier
C) Nepal's refusal to join SAARC
D) Nepal's support for the LTTE
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Nepal's warm relations with China
Why: India has been uneasy about Nepal's close ties with China, among other issues.
Why not the others:
(B) Siachen is an India–Pakistan issue.
(C) Nepal is a SAARC member.
(D) Nepal did not support the LTTE.
Key point: India and Nepal share close but sometimes uneasy ties.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.sub_topic: Where Russia has supported India
questions.question: On which of the following issues has Russia supported India?
options: A) India's claim to a seat in the G-7
C) India's membership of the European Union
D) India's request to join the Warsaw Pact
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) India's position on Kashmir
Why: Russia has supported India on Kashmir, as well as on terrorism and energy supplies.
Why not the others:
(A) Russia has not taken up such a claim.
(C) India cannot join the EU.
(D) The Warsaw Pact no longer exists.
Key point: Russia has been a reliable partner for India.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.sub_topic: The 1971 election — the false claim
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) The opposition Grand Alliance's main common slogan was 'Indira Hatao'.
(B) The Congress (R) on its own won 352 Lok Sabha seats in 1971.
(C) The 1971 Lok Sabha election was held before it was due.
(D) The Grand Alliance won a majority in the 1971 election.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (D) only
Why: Only (D) is false: Indira Gandhi's Congress (R) won a huge majority, and the Grand Alliance was routed.
Why not the others: (A) the opposition's slogan was 'Indira Hatao'. (B) the Congress (R) won 352 seats. (C) Indira Gandhi had the Lok Sabha dissolved early, in December 1970. Options (A), (B) and (C) name a true statement as false.
Key point: 1971 restored the Congress under Indira Gandhi.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Politics of Planned Development
questions.sub_topic: Regions that gained most from the Green Revolution
questions.question: Which regions benefited most from the Green Revolution?
options: A) Kerala, Tamil Nadu and coastal Karnataka
B) Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
C) Bihar, Odisha and the hill districts of Bengal
D) Assam, Manipur and the other north-eastern States
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
Why: The Green Revolution brought the largest gains to areas with irrigation, mainly Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.
Why not the others: (A), (C), (D) These regions gained much less.
Key point: The Green Revolution widened gaps between regions.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Alternative Centres of Economic and Political Power
questions.sub_topic: When China may overtake the US economy
questions.question: NCERT notes projections that China will overtake the United States as the world's largest economy by about:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 2040
Why: China's economy was projected to overtake the USA's by about 2040.
Why not the others: (A), (C), (D) These dates do not match the projection.
Key point: China's growth is reshaping the world economy.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Regional Aspirations and Conflicts
questions.sub_topic: Regional demands and outcomes
questions.question:
Match List-I (Region or group) with List-II (Demand or outcome).

List-I
(A) Goa
(B) Sikkim
(C) The Bodos
(D) The DMK

List-II
(I) Became a State of India in 1975
(II) Won power in Madras State in 1967
(III) Demanded autonomy within Assam
(IV) Voted in a 1967 opinion poll to stay separate from Maharashtra
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(II)
Why: Goa's opinion poll of 1967 rejected a merger with Maharashtra (IV). Sikkim became a State of India in 1975 (I). The Bodos demanded autonomy within Assam (III). The DMK won power in Madras in 1967 (II).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps Goa and Sikkim. Option (B) swaps Sikkim and the Bodos. Option (D) swaps the Bodos and the DMK.
Key point: Regional demands were met in many different ways.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Era of One-Party Dominance
questions.sub_topic: First Indian Governor-General
questions.question: Who was the first Indian Governor-General of independent India and later a founder of the Swatantra Party?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) C. Rajagopalachari
Why: C. Rajagopalachari became the first Indian Governor-General and later founded the Swatantra Party.
Why not the others:
(A) Rajendra Prasad was the first President.
(B) Patel was Deputy Prime Minister.
(C) Kripalani led the KMPP.
Key point: Rajaji moved from the Congress to the opposition.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Globalisation and Its Critics
questions.sub_topic: Why some argue globalisation is not new
questions.question: Why do some scholars argue that globalisation is not new?
options: A) Because the internet has existed in some form for several centuries
B) Because India had trade and cultural links abroad for centuries
C) Because the WTO was founded way back in the eighteenth century
D) Because all countries shared one common currency in ancient times
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Because India had trade and cultural links abroad for centuries
Why: India and other regions had long-standing links of trade, ideas and people across the world, long before modern globalisation.
Why not the others:
(A) The internet is recent.
(C) The WTO was founded in 1995.
(D) There was no single ancient currency.
Key point: Globalisation has a long history, though its present speed is new.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Recent Issues and Challenges
questions.sub_topic: Reforms and reservations in the 1990s — which hold
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) India faced a severe economic crisis in 1991.
(B) The Supreme Court upheld the decision to reserve central government jobs for OBCs.
(C) 27 per cent of central government jobs were reserved for the OBCs.
(D) The Mandal recommendations were implemented by the Rajiv Gandhi government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A) the 1991 crisis led to the New Economic Policy. (B) the Supreme Court upheld OBC reservation. (C) the reservation was 27 per cent.
Why not the others: (D) is false: the National Front government of V.P. Singh implemented the Mandal recommendations in 1990. Options (C) and (D) include (D); option (A) leaves out (C).
Key point: Economic reform and Mandal reshaped politics at the same time.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: South Asia in the Post-Cold War Era
questions.sub_topic: Democracy and conflict across South Asia — spot the error
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) India and Pakistan have agreed on confidence-building measures to reduce the risk of war.
(B) Bangladesh has never had military rule since it became independent.
(C) Nepal was once a Hindu kingdom.
(D) The Sri Lankan armed forces defeated the LTTE in 2009.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B) only
Why: Only (B) is false: Bangladesh came under military rule after 1975 and returned to elected government in 1991.
Why not the others: (A) the two countries have agreed on confidence-building measures. (C) Nepal was a Hindu kingdom. (D) the LTTE was defeated in 2009. Options (A), (C) and (D) name a true statement as false.
Key point: South Asia has seen both military rule and democratic revival.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Security in the Contemporary World
questions.sub_topic: Arms control and terrorism, 1972–2001, in order
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
(A) The Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty
(B) The Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty
(C) The attacks of 11 September in the USA
(D) The second Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty (SALT II)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (B), (D), (A), (C)
Why: (B) The ABM Treaty was signed in 1972. (D) SALT II was signed in 1979. (A) The CTBT came in 1996. (C) The 9/11 attacks took place in 2001.
Why not the others: Option (A) puts SALT II before the ABM Treaty. Option (B) puts the CTBT before SALT II. Option (C) puts 2001 before 1996.
Key point: 1972 → 1979 → 1996 → 2001.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.sub_topic: Why the UN still matters in a unipolar world
questions.question: Why does NCERT argue that the UN still matters in a world dominated by one superpower?
options: A) It brings states together and helps them deal with the superpower.
B) It has its own army, stronger than that of the superpower.
C) It can veto the decisions of any national government.
D) It owns and controls most of the world's oil supply.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) It brings states together and helps them deal with the superpower.
Why: The UN offers a forum where states can talk with, and sometimes restrain, the dominant power.
Why not the others:
(B) The UN has no army of its own of that kind.
(C) Vetoes belong to the five permanent members, not the UN.
(D) The UN does not control oil.
Key point: The UN is imperfect but indispensable.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Crises of the Constitutional Order
questions.sub_topic: Change made by the 42nd Amendment to the term of legislatures
questions.question: The 42nd Amendment, passed during the Emergency, extended the term of the Lok Sabha and the State Assemblies from five years to:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) six years

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Globalisation and Its Critics
questions.sub_topic: Globalisation in India — the false claim
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) India began to globalise its economy right after Independence, in 1947.
(B) Foreign investment in India rose after the reforms.
(C) In India, resistance to globalisation has come from both the left and the right.
(D) The reforms of 1991 removed many controls on trade and investment.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A) only
Why: Only (A) is false: after 1947 India followed protectionism; it opened its economy from 1991.
Why not the others: (B) foreign investment grew after the reforms. (C) both left and right groups have resisted. (D) the 1991 reforms removed many controls. Options (B), (C) and (D) name a true statement as false.
Key point: India's globalisation is a story of the years after 1991.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Nation-Building and Its Problems
questions.sub_topic: Terms of nation-building
questions.question:
Match List-I (Term) with List-II (Meaning).

List-I
(A) Two-nation theory
(B) Linguistic State
(C) Princely state
(D) Refugee

List-II
(I) A person forced to flee home because of violence or persecution
(II) A state ruled by a prince under British paramountcy
(III) The idea that Hindus and Muslims were two separate nations
(IV) A State whose boundaries follow the language of its people
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: The two-nation theory said Hindus and Muslims were separate nations (III). A linguistic State follows language (IV). A princely state was ruled by a prince under British paramountcy (II). A refugee is forced to flee (I).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps the two-nation theory and the linguistic State. Option (C) swaps the linguistic State and the princely state. Option (D) swaps the princely state and the refugee.
Key point: Each term names a challenge India faced after 1947.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: India's External Relations
questions.sub_topic: One of the three aims of Nehru's foreign policy
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Jawaharlal Nehru, who shaped independent India's foreign policy, set it three broad aims: to preserve the sovereignty won after a long struggle, to protect the country's territorial integrity, and to promote rapid economic development. He chose non-alignment as the way to achieve them. Non-alignment did not mean staying away from world affairs or being neutral on every question. It meant keeping out of the military alliances of both Cold War blocs and judging each issue on its merits. Even before Independence, India hosted the Asian Relations Conference in New Delhi in March 1947. It backed Indonesia's struggle for freedom from Dutch rule and in 1949 convened an international conference in its support. With leaders such as Tito of Yugoslavia, Nasser of Egypt, Sukarno of Indonesia and Nkrumah of Ghana, Nehru went on to found the Non-Aligned Movement. Staying outside the blocs also let India receive economic and technical help from both the United States and the Soviet Union. Critics complained that non-alignment was unprincipled and that India often avoided taking a firm stand. Its defenders replied that it gave a newly independent and poor country the freedom to decide for itself.

Question: Which of the following is one of the three aims of India's foreign policy named in the passage?
options: A) Spreading socialism to other Asian countries
B) Joining the Western military alliance
D) Building the largest navy in Asia
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Promoting rapid economic development
Why: The passage names three aims: preserving sovereignty, protecting territorial integrity and promoting rapid economic development.
Why not the others:
(A) Spreading socialism is not named.
(B) India stayed out of military alliances.
(D) A large navy is not mentioned.
Key point: Foreign policy served the goals of a new and developing nation.

options: A) Non-alignment meant keeping out of the military alliances of both blocs.

Question: Based on the passage, how did non-alignment help India's economic development?
